blocks.content: Union Territories are administrative divisions ruled directly by the Union Government of India.

rows: President through Administrator or Lt. Governor
Present only in Delhi, Puducherry, and J&K

items: Article 239AA was created by the 69th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1991, conferring special status to Delhi as the National Capital Territory.
Parliament can make laws on any subject in the State List for Union Territories without needing constitutional amendment procedures.
Delhi and Jammu & Kashmir are the only Union Territories with independent High Courts.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: States share a federal relationship with the Centre with distributed legislative powers, whereas Union Territories are under direct central administration.
Articles 239 to 241 under Part VIII of the Indian Constitution deal with the governance and administration of Union Territories.
The President administers Union Territories through an Administrator or Lieutenant Governor appointed by them.
Puducherry, Delhi, and Jammu & Kashmir are Union Territories that possess their own elected Legislative Assemblies.
Parliament holds ultimate authority to make laws on subjects in any of the three lists for Union Territories.
